checks.message: Enforce encryption for query results in the workgroup configuration
checks.context: Athena writes query results to S3. Without enforcing encryption in the workgroup, results can land in plaintext. Set EncryptionConfiguration to SSE_KMS and enforce it so users can't override it.

checks.message: Verify the query has a partition filter - full table scans on large datasets cost real money
checks.context: A full scan on a multi-TB S3 dataset can cost hundreds of dollars in a single query. Always filter on partition columns and use LIMIT during development.

checks.message: No security configuration - encryption and Kerberos are disabled by default
checks.context: Without a security configuration, EMR has no at-rest encryption, no in-transit encryption, and no Kerberos auth. Any node in the cluster can read all HDFS data. Create a security configuration with encryption enabled before running production workloads.

checks.message: Verify the cluster is in private subnets - EMR master nodes in public subnets are internet-reachable
checks.context: The Hadoop web UIs (HDFS NameNode on 50070, YARN on 8088) have no authentication by default. A public master node exposes your entire cluster to the internet.

checks.message: Verify all output has been written to S3 before terminating
checks.context: Terminating an EMR cluster destroys all HDFS data immediately. Any intermediate results not yet written to S3 are permanently lost.

checks.message: Verify the stream has server-side encryption enabled
checks.context: Kinesis Data Streams supports SSE with KMS. Without it, records are stored in plaintext in the stream. Encryption is enabled via a separate `kinesis start-stream-encryption` call after stream creation - not at create time.

checks.message: Stream deletion destroys all unprocessed records immediately
checks.context: All data in the stream is permanently deleted, including records within the retention window. Any consumers that haven't processed those records will miss them permanently.
Amazon Data Firehose buffers data before delivering to S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch. Without SSE, that buffered data is in plaintext. Enable encryption for streams carrying PII or financial data.

checks.message: Scope the job role to only the data sources and destinations this job touches
checks.context: Glue jobs with s3:* can access every bucket in your account. A misconfigured or compromised job can exfiltrate your entire data lake. Scope to specific bucket ARNs.

checks.message: Never hardcode credentials in Glue job scripts
checks.context: Glue scripts are stored in S3 and visible to anyone with S3 read access to that bucket. Use Glue connections with Secrets Manager references or IAM roles for all data source auth.

checks.message: Verify no active runs or triggers depend on this job before deleting
checks.context: Deleting a running Glue job terminates it immediately. Triggers and workflows that reference this job will fail on their next execution.

checks.message: Extended retention incurs additional charges per shard-hour
checks.context: Default retention is 24 hours (included). Extended retention up to 7 days and long-term retention up to 365 days incur per-shard-hour charges. Verify the cost impact for high-shard-count streams.

checks.message: Verify the application IAM role is not being broadened beyond required resources
checks.context: Kinesis Analytics applications process streaming data and need access to source and destination resources. A role with overly broad permissions can be exploited to access unrelated data streams or S3 buckets.
